coupling.design: one plate per tray at its back right corner, facing out through the right-hand side; an actuated dock in the side wall of each slot a tray uses and of the bay; stroke 45 mm across the tray's travel

media.coupling: 4 x O3 mm power units, 39 A each

coupling.why_not_the_back_edge: in a front-column slot and at the opening the back edge faces the shaft; a dock there would sit in the 106-146 mm between the tray and the extractor's platform, in the path of every tray it pulls, and at the opening the shutter is 35 mm behind the tray
sequence: shut and vent air, N2 and water (CombiTac: no mating or parting under pressure)
bay dock pushes in, pins first
contacts mate, supplies open, back on mains

ask_kardex: The heat a tray may give off in a slot, and in total, and the interior temperature the drives and controls are rated for.
Whether a column can be ventilated (a filtered fan and an outlet on the roof), and whether a furnace at 650 C may run inside at all.
The extractor's repeatability at a slot, for a dock that takes 4 mm of misalignment.
Whether the side walls can take a window and a dock behind the supports at a slot, and the space between the column wall and the cladding (taken here as about 105 mm).
Whether power to a slot can stay on while a tray is stored, and what they would fit (the dealer offered a quick-connect cord).

tether.note: The line has to stay in the 30 mm between the tray's side and the extractor's guide rails, the shutter needs a notch for it, and while the tray is out the line spans the shaft, so the extractor can't fetch any other tray. It suits one tray stored at the opening's own height.
tether.source: igus e-spool flex 2.0: extension up to 15 m, cables 5-15 mm, spring (SP, SB) or crank; 'No slip ring: Uninterrupted supply of power, data and air.' igus e-spool power: motor-driven, up to 25 m, 1.2 m/s, power, data, fibre, air and liquids, no slip ring (igus.com).
